issue.title: Issue #432: Attention view: group resource and input waits apart from approval
issue.text:
Issue #432: Attention view: group resource and input waits apart from approval
State: open
Labels: class/bug, size/M, pipeline/default
body_sha256: 15df027abbdbd04730efeb9889d0084d5a86d0ee4a0332c165b01cc1dc5fddcb

--- body ---
Follow-up to #376, from the af review of step 10 of #384 (Task `ux-s10-attention-1`; the code is in PR #429). On 27 October 2026 the owner decided that only blockers are fixed before a tier merges. This finding is not a blocker. Line numbers are at commit 94bc0a83.

## Finding

**The attention view says a Task that needs resources or input is waiting for approval** (major; correctness reviewer; the evaluator passed the step).
- `TaskAttentionV1::of` (`crates/review-core/src/task/state.rs:483`) puts every `planned` and `waiting` Task in the `approval` group, titled "Waiting for approval".
- The refresh path also records `waiting` for a Task that needs resources (an infeasible selection) or input (missing facts) (`crates/af/src/task_execution/refresh.rs:250-283`).
- Its next command is then `af task plan --file TASK_FILE --fit` or `af task show ID` (`crates/af/src/task_execution/state.rs:145-155`), not an approval.
- The CLI (`af task list --attention`), the TUI's attention rows, the `af/task-attention@1` JSON group and the table in `docs/tasks.md:359` all show such a Task as awaiting approval.
- Issue #376 asks for Tasks grouped by what they wait for.

Fix: give resource and input waits a group of their own, derived from the same state and next action. Keep `approval` for a plan to confirm or review. Change the CLI, TUI, schema, help and docs together. Add an execution-path test that produces a `NeedsResources` or `NeedsInput` Task and checks its text, JSON and TUI group.

--- comment 1: PakhomovAlexander (owner), 2026-10-30T12:10:41Z ---
**Triage:** `class/bug` `size/M` → `pipeline/default`. Resource and input waits are labelled as approval, violating the stated behavior of grouping Tasks by what they wait for; bug takes precedence over agent and human experience. The rubric explicitly treats this additive group under af/task-attention@1 as M. PR #429 introduced the attention view but provides no explicit evidence that this correction shipped.
**Resolution:** Astra open, Opus open (evidence: crates/review-core/src/task/state.rs:483, crates/af/src/task_execution/refresh.rs:250-283, crates/af/src/task_execution/state.rs:145-155, PR #429, docs/tasks.md:359).
**Acceptance:** Resource and input waits appear in a group separate from plan confirmation or review across CLI text, TUI and af/task-attention@1 JSON, with matching schema, help and documentation and an execution-path test producing NeedsResources or NeedsInput and verifying all three views.

  465  /// What a Task waits for, as `af task list --attention` and the browser's Tasks pane group it:
  466  /// a pure reading of its [`TaskStateV1`] (phase, outcome, cause and whether it names a next
  467  /// command), never recorded. Every state is in exactly one group; the first five need a person,
  468  /// [`TaskAttentionV1::Running`] and [`TaskAttentionV1::Nothing`] do not.
  469  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  470  #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
  471  pub enum TaskAttentionV1 {
  472      /// A plan waits for `af task run --confirm-plan`, or the Task waits for a plan review,
  473      /// resources, input or a decision.
  474      Approval,
  475      /// A required check of the gate failed or could not run.
  476      GateFailed,
  477      /// The review or the evaluator asked for changes.
  478      Findings,
  479      /// Verified, with a result `af task deliver` has not delivered yet.
  480      Deliver,
  481      /// It stopped on a Provider, an interrupt, a limit or its wall clock.
  482      Stopped,
  483      /// A writer runs it now; it names no command until it settles.
  484      Running,
  485      /// Nothing to run: delivered, verified with nothing to deliver, or collected.
  486      Nothing,
  487  }
  488  
  489  impl TaskAttentionV1 {
  490      /// Every group, in the order `af task list --attention` prints them.
  491      pub const ALL: [Self; 7] = [
  492          Self::Approval,
  493          Self::GateFailed,
  494          Self::Findings,
  495          Self::Deliver,
  496          Self::Stopped,
  497          Self::Running,
  498          Self::Nothing,
  499      ];
  500  
  501      /// The group a Task in `state` belongs to. A collected Task names no command and needs
  502      /// nothing, whatever outcome its tombstone retained.
  503      pub fn of(state: &TaskStateV1) -> Self {
  504          if state.cause == Some(TaskCauseV1::Collected) {
  505              return Self::Nothing;
  506          }
  507          match (state.phase, state.outcome) {
  508              (TaskStatePhaseV1::Running, _) => Self::Running,
  509              (TaskStatePhaseV1::Planned | TaskStatePhaseV1::Waiting, _) => Self::Approval,
  510              (_, Some(TaskOutcomeV1::Verified)) if state.next_action.is_some() => Self::Deliver,
  511              (_, Some(TaskOutcomeV1::Verified)) => Self::Nothing,
  512              (_, Some(TaskOutcomeV1::GateFailed)) => Self::GateFailed,
  513              (_, Some(TaskOutcomeV1::ChangesRequested)) => Self::Findings,

docs/tasks.md:359 (named by the issue body), lines 329-389 of this Snapshot:
  329  
  330  Every state that ended names the one command to run next: the last line of `af task show` and
  331  `af task run` (`next: af task run ID --retry-gate`), `none` when there is none, and
  332  `state.next_action` under `--json`. It is `af task findings ID` after reviewer findings,
  333  `af task run ID --retry-gate` after a failed gate that the kernel can run again on the same
  334  candidate ([Retry a failed gate](#retry-a-failed-gate)), whatever its cause, `af task show ID
  335  --checks` after one it cannot, `af task run ID` to resume a cancelled run (`af task start --file
  336  TASK_FILE` once its interrupted node used up its recovery allowance), `af task plan --file
  337  TASK_FILE --fit` after a budget or deadline ran out (with a new `task_id` once the Task ran),
  338  `af provider status` or `af provider setup ID --login` after a Provider failure (`af provider
  339  status` after `provider_environment`, an environment failure such as identity probes that proved
  340  nothing after their retries, never an account change), and `af task run NEW_TASK_ID --from ID`
  341  after `attempt_wall` when the Worker its wall stopped left edits
  342  ([An Attempt wall keeps the edits](#an-attempt-wall-keeps-the-edits)), else `af task show ID`. A command given
  343  `--repo`, `--state` or `--workspace` prints an `af task` next command with them as typed, so it
  344  runs as printed against the same Store; under the default Store it carries none. `af task show`
  345  prints, per
  346  failed node, its cause, the first line of its error and the artifact IDs of its whole diagnostic
  347  and stderr; a node that only lacks the receipt of a branch that failed comes after that branch.
  348  A command that exits with an outcome's code while its result goes to stdout, such as `af task
  349  explain` or `af task run` of a Task that already finished, ends with the same line on stderr as
  350  the run log does, `Task ID: finished/gate_failed/check_failed; next: af task run ID --retry-gate`:
  351  a non-zero exit always says why on stderr.
  352  
  353  `af task show ID --checks` prints the gate's last check receipt: each check's status, duration,
  354  warm or cold directories, its warm layer when the policy has `[warm]` (the key, how the check came
  355  by it, the source groups it rebuilt, its build and test phases and an eviction with its cause,
  356  [Warm checks](task-execution/warm-checks.md)), the step that stopped it, its failing and flaky
  357  tests and the last 40 lines of its stderr; `--json` prints one
  358  [`af/task-checks@3`](../schemas/task-checks-v3.json) document. The gate's failed and flaky tests
  359  and the step that stopped a check come from its report when the check writes one, and from the
  360  text scan of its output only for a check without one (absent or refused): the runner's `FAIL`,
  361  `TIMEOUT` and `SIGABRT` lines, its `flaky:` lines and its step log. A check line that prints this
  362  evidence ends with where it came from, `evidence: report` or `evidence: output`
  363  ([ADR-0258](adr/0258-task-gate-evidence-comes-from-the-check-report.md)). `af task list --json`
  364  rows carry the same `gate` summary, and after a failed gate `af task run` names the failing
  365  tests, at most 20, then `… and N more; af task show ID --checks`.
  366  
  367  A check the kernel stopped at its wall (its per-check wall, its check Attempt's wall or a warm
  368  phase deadline, whichever bound its process) is recorded as such in the
  369  [`af/TaskCheckReceipt@2`](../schemas/task-check-receipt-v2.json) under `stopped`: the cause
  370  `wall`, the wall it ran under and how long it ran
  371  ([ADR-0255](adr/0255-say-a-check-stopped-at-its-wall-and-carry-typed-acceptance-in-the-check-receipt.md)).
  372  The Task ends `finished/gate_failed/check_failed`, never `preflight_failed`, and `af task show`
  373  (`why:`), `af task show --checks` (with `stop` under `--json`), `af task report` (the row's
  374  detail) and the run's stderr each say `check kernel stopped at its 90 min wall after 88 min` and
  375  what to do: make the check faster, or raise its wall in `.af/code-policy.toml`
  376  (`check_wall_ms`, `check_process_wall_ms` or `[warm] build_wall_ms`) and plan the Task again;
  377  `af task run ID --retry-gate` runs it again under the same wall. The wall is what the check's
  378  process ran under, so it is what was left of the check's wall after preparation. Only a check that
  379  did not start still says `never started`.
  380  
  381  A Task's wall clock starts at its first `af task run`, not when it is planned: the preview says
  382  `deadline starts when you run`, the Store moves the recorded deadline by the time the Task waited
  383  for that run, so the confirmed plan is exactly the plan that runs, and the run prints the
  384  deadline in local time with the time left (`deadline 17:41:18 +03 (2 h 59 min from now)`);
  385  `af task show --json` carries it as `clock`. `af task plan` of a Task file whose content and bindings equal the planned Task's prints
  386  the existing plan; a changed file under a planned ID is refused, and `af task plan --replace`
  387  plans an unstarted Task again in place. A plan the Task's limits are too small for is refused

rubric.title: Issue triage design, sections 4 and 5
rubric.text:
## 4. Labels

Every triage label is namespaced. The namespace is for parsing; the value is for reading. The
triage runner and the owner set these; nobody else does.

| Namespace | Values | Cardinality | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class/` | `bug`, `perf`, `feature`, `aix`, `uix`, `sdlc`, `security`, `docs`, `research`, `decision` | exactly one | What kind of work it is |
| `size/` | `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL` | exactly one | Effort by the rubric in §5 |
| `pipeline/` | `light`, `default`, `design`, `hand` | exactly one | Which af pipeline, hence which model, takes it |
| `triage/` | `pending`, `needs-info`, `disputed`, `maybe-fixed`, `duplicate`, `held` | zero or one | Process state |

Class definitions:

- `bug`: af does something other than its documentation, contract or ADR says.
- `perf`: a measured cost (time, tokens, disk, memory) that is higher than it should be, with
  the number in the issue. A wrong number is a `bug`.
- `feature`: a capability or contract that does not exist.
- `aix`: agent experience, the ergonomics of af for an agent that drives it: output shapes,
  next-action lines, JSON documents, prompts.
- `uix`: human experience: the TUI, help text, first screens, onboarding.
- `sdlc`: tests, CI, gates, release, repository process, test speed and flakes.
- `security`: a trust-boundary defect. The runner never labels or comments on one in public;
  see §7.
- `docs`: documentation alone.
- `research`: a study whose output is a report, not code.
- `decision`: nothing moves until the owner chooses; the comment names the choice.

**Precedence.** The definitions overlap (#432 is a contract bug, an agent-facing JSON shape
and a TUI screen at once; #211 is a measured gate latency and a gate process change). A triager
takes the first matching class in this order: `security`; `decision` when the issue is
explicitly blocked on an owner choice; `research` for a report-only deliverable; `docs` for a
documentation-only change; `bug` for violated documented behaviour, except that measured
excessive resource consumption is `perf` unless the measurement itself is wrong; `perf`; `aix`;
`uix`; `sdlc`; `feature`. When several experience or process classes match, the class is the
one named by the issue's primary acceptance criterion, ties broken in the listed order; the
others are named in the rationale. There is no `area/` namespace (owner decision, 2026-10-30):
where an issue lives is derived at read time from the author's repository citations, whose first
path component names the crate or script directory.

`triage/` states:

- `pending`: not yet triaged, or re-triage requested.
- `needs-info`: the triager could not reach a confident class or size; the comment asks one
  concrete question. A reply from anyone re-enters the queue (§6.6).
- `disputed`: the two triagers disagree on class or size; the comment carries both rationales.
  An owner label on the disputed namespace resolves it (§6.5).
- `maybe-fixed`: the weekly sweep found an explicit completed-fix reference on `main`; the
  comment carries the evidence.
- `duplicate`: both triagers named the same open issue as the subject; the comment names it.
- `held`: the issue is under private owner review (§7) and no runner touches it.

Existing labels migrate once, by script: `Agent UX Improvement` becomes `class/aix`; `test-perf`
becomes `class/sdlc`; `bug` and `enhancement` stay as the labels the outside
templates apply, and triage replaces them with `class/bug` and `class/feature`. The PR labels
(`test:*`, `release:*`, `no-*`) are unchanged: they select validation classes on pull requests
and are not issue labels.

## 5. The size rubric

The rubric is what makes two models and the owner reach the same estimate. Sizes are evaluated
in descending order, `XL`, `L`, `M`, `S`, and the first match wins. Insufficient evidence
produces `needs-info`, never an invented size.

| Size | Test, in order | Default pipeline | Model and reviewers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `XL` | Needs a design document and owner decisions before any code. | `design` | Design rounds with the owner; no implementation Task until the design is accepted |
| `L` | Changes a contract, schema version, budget or sandbox boundary, or needs several Tasks. | `design` | A workstream: one design review by Astra xhigh before the first implementing Task, then `default` per Task |
| `M` | Everything understood well enough to implement that is not `L` or `S`: two or three crates, a new fixture or test class, an additive field under an existing document version, a new or amended ADR that records a bounded change. | `default` (`default/implementation`, ADR-0253) | Opus 5.5 high implementer; Terra bugs and Sol correctness reviewers (Sol required); Astra medium gate-quality reviewer; Astra high evaluator. Findings from every bound reviewer count toward convergence |
| `S` | All of: one module; repro present or derivable from the evidence; no schema, contract or budget change; no new fixture or test class; no ADR. | `light` (`default-light/implementation`, ADR-0262) | Opus 5.5 medium implementer, correctness reviewer, evaluator |

Two rules the check enforces mechanically (§6.3):

- A proposed contract, schema-version, budget or sandbox-boundary change forces at least `L`.
  Citing an existing ADR as evidence of expected behaviour does not affect size; a needed new
  or amended ADR is recorded in the document's `adr` field and makes `S` impossible, so the
  Task that writes it runs on `default` at least.
- `pipeline/` follows size (`S` to `light`, `M` to `default`, `L` and `XL` to `design`) unless
  the owner has set `pipeline/hand`, for a configuration edit, a documentation line or a GitHub
  action where a model Task would cost more than the change. The triager may propose `hand` in
  its rationale; only the owner sets it.

The hand triage of 2026-10-30 (`review-context/hand-triage-2026-10-30.json`) is a baseline for
calibration, not expected output under this rubric. Its "easy" set (#474, #432, #430, #355,
#211, #207, #199, #139) is re-evaluated by the rules above before any count is published: #474
amends ADR-0170's deadline semantics, so it is at least `M` with `adr` set; #432 adds a group to
the `af/task-attention@1` document, an additive field under the existing version, so `M`; the
rest stay candidates for `S` until a triager confirms the repro.
